tf.passage: What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. tf.passage: One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs. The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause.

tf.passage: In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair. The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.

tf.passage: When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things. The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer. By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.

read.ko: 스터디 그룹 모임에 가는 길에 Liz는 실수로 노트북을 길에 떨어뜨려 그것을 심하게 손상시켰다.
read.en: On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it.

read.ko: 그것은 여전히 켜지기는 하지만, 화면에 금이 갔고 몇몇 키는 작동하지 않는다.
read.en: Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working.

read.ko: 그녀는 그것을 수리받을 수 있지만, 그렇게 하기를 망설이고 있다.
read.en: She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so.

read.ko: 때때로 수리는 비용이 많이 들고, 보통 오랜 시간이 걸린다.
read.en: Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time.

read.ko: 게다가 그 노트북은 5년 정도 되었다.
read.en: Besides, the laptop is about five years old.

read.ko: 이 경우, 오래된 것을 버리고 새것을 구입하는 것이 더 합리적인 선택처럼 보일 수도 있다.
read.en: In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option.

read.ko: 하지만 실제로는 그것이 최선의 방법이 아닐 수도 있다.
read.en: In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do.

read.ko: 만약 Liz가 노트북을 쓰레기통에 버린다면, 그녀는 전자 쓰레기라는 심각한 문제에 기여하게 될 것이다.
read.en: If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste.

read.ko: 전자 쓰레기란 정확히 무엇인가?
read.en: What exactly is e-waste?

read.ko: 이 용어는 버려진 전자 장치와 전기 기기를 가리킨다.
read.en: The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances.

read.ko: 납과 같이 이 제품들에 들어 있는 유독성 물질 때문에, 전자 쓰레기는 심각한 건강 및 환경 위험 요소이다.
read.en: Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard.

read.ko: 설상가상으로, 매년 발생하는 전자 쓰레기의 양은 걱정스러운 속도로 증가하고 있다.
read.en: To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate.

read.ko: 2021년에 전 세계적으로 총 5,740만 메트릭톤의 전자 쓰레기가 발생했는데, 이는 전자 쓰레기에 관한 자료가 처음 수집된 해인 2014년에 비해 37% 증가한 것이었다.
read.en: In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected.

read.ko: 전문가들은 2030년이면 매년 발생하는 전자 쓰레기의 양이 단 16년 만에 두 배가 될 것이라고 예측한다.
read.en: Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years.

read.ko: 이러한 이유로 이 문제를 해결하기 위한 노력이 이루어지고 있는데, 그중 대부분은 제품을 수리하기 더 쉽게 만드는 데 초점을 맞추고 있다.
read.en: For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair.

read.ko: 전 세계의 몇 가지 현실적인 접근법을 살펴보자.
read.en: Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.

read.ko: 많은 사람이 고장 난 장치를 버리는 한 가지 이유는 그것들이 수리하기에 너무 어렵기 때문이다.
read.en: One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair.

read.ko: 예를 들어, 어떤 장치는 분해하기 어려울 수 있고, 또는 그 제조사가 그것을 고치려면 공식 서비스 센터로 가져올 것을 요구할 수도 있다.
read.en: For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed.

read.ko: 많은 회사는 고객들이 고장 난 물건을 제3자 수리점에 가져가는 것을 허용하지 않는다.
read.en: Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops.

read.ko: 게다가, 일부 제품은 의도적으로 수리하기 어렵게 설계된다.
read.en: What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair.

read.ko: 소비자들이 물건을 고치는 방법에 대한 설명서나 수리를 완료하는 데 필요한 부품을 구하지 못하는 것은 흔한 일이다.
read.en: It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs.

read.ko: 수리할 권리 운동은 다음 내용을 명시하는 법률 제정을 추진함으로써 이러한 문제들을 해결하려 하고 있다: 만약 당신이 어떤 제품을 소유하고 있다면, 당신은 그것을 직접 고치거나 당신이 선택한 기술자에게 가져갈 권리가 있다.
read.en: The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice.

read.ko: 소비자의 권리를 보호하기 위해, 수리할 권리 운동은 네 가지를 요구한다.
read.en: To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things.

read.ko: 둘째, 개인을 포함한 제3자가 수리에 필요한 부품과 도구를 구할 수 있어야 한다.
read.en: Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs.

read.ko: 셋째, 소비자들이 자신의 장치에 맞춤형 소프트웨어를 설치하지 못하게 막는 관행은 법으로 금지되어야 한다.
read.en: Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law.

read.ko: 마지막으로, 그것은 제조사들이 수리를 최대한 쉽게 만드는 방식으로 장치를 설계할 것을 요구한다.
read.en: Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible.

read.ko: 이 운동의 지지자들은 이 모든 목표가 이루어진다면 훨씬 적은 전자 쓰레기가 발생할 것이라고 말한다.
read.en: Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated.

read.ko: 그들의 노력 덕분에, 미국의 40개가 넘는 주가 수리할 권리 법률 제정에 착수했다.
read.en: Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation.

read.ko: 이 운동은 점점 더 많은 국가가 그 대의에 동참하면서 유럽에서도 영향력이 커지고 있다.
read.en: This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause.

read.ko: 2021년 1월, 프랑스 정부는 모든 제조사가 스마트폰, 노트북, 세탁기, 텔레비전, 잔디 깎는 기계라는 다섯 가지 종류의 전자 장치와 전기 기기에 ‘수리 가능성 지수’를 표기하도록 요구하는 법안을 통과시켰다.
read.en: In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers.

read.ko: 0에서 10까지의 점수와 색상으로 구분된 체계를 사용하여, 그 지수는 소비자들이 제품을 구매하기 전에 그것이 얼마나 쉽게 수리될 수 있는지 알 수 있게 해 준다.
read.en: Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it.

read.ko: 그 지수는 수리 정보의 이용 가능성, 분해의 용이성, 예비 부품의 가격을 포함한 여러 요소를 고려한다.
read.en: The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts.

read.ko: 밝은 빨간색 라벨의 낮은 숫자는 그 제품을 수리하는 것이 어려울 것이라는 의미인 반면, 초록색 라벨의 높은 숫자는 그 제품이 수리하기 쉽다는 것을 나타낸다.
read.en: A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair.

read.ko: 그 지수는 두 가지 긍정적인 효과를 가지도록 고안되었다.
read.en: The index was designed to have two positive effects.

read.ko: 첫째, 그것은 소비자들이 새 장치와 기기를 구매할 때 정보에 근거한 결정을 내릴 수 있게 해 준다.
read.en: Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances.

read.ko: 둘째, 그것은 제조사들이 자사 제품을 더 수리하기 쉽게 만들도록 장려한다.
read.en: Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair.

read.ko: 그 결과, 더 적은 전자·전기 제품이 쓰레기 매립지로 가게 되면서, 프랑스는 가까운 미래에 더 지속 가능한 사회로 전환하는 것을 기대할 수 있다.
read.en: As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future.

read.ko: 그러나 그 지수의 영향은 프랑스를 훨씬 넘어 퍼질 가능성이 있다.
read.en: The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France.

read.ko: 우리는 세계 경제 속에 살고 있으며, 프랑스 시장에서 자사 기기를 판매하고자 하는 모든 회사는 수리 가능성 지수에 따라 제품에 라벨을 붙여야 할 것이다.
read.en: We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index.

read.ko: 그 지수가 성공한다면, 우리는 전 세계의 더 많은 나라가 프랑스의 혁신적인 선례를 따르는 것을 보게 되리라 기대할 수 있다.
read.en: If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.

read.ko: 소비자들에게 약간의 유용한 조언과 함께 알맞은 도구와 재료가 주어지면, 그들은 전자 제품에 발생하는 손상의 상당 부분을 스스로 수리할 수 있다.
read.en: When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves.

para.en: On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste.

What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world. *metric ton 메트릭톤(1,000kg을 1톤으로 하는 중량 단위)

One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs. The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause.

In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair. The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.

When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things. The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer. By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.

Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, and she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score. In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
